title: A 309-Million-Year-Old Creature Gets a Name — and a Tribute
summary:
A fossil found in Illinois years ago has turned out to be a brand-new species — a strange creature that lived 309 million years ago, long before the dinosaurs.

The species is called Jeanerpeton mazonensis, which means 'Jean's crawler from Mazon Creek.' It honors the mothers of the two student scientists who helped identify it — both named Jean.

The animal, an early relative of modern amphibians, looked like a salamander with the short, stocky body of a frog. It lived during the Carboniferous period, when the area around present-day Chicago was a warm, swampy river delta.

The fossil comes from Mazon Creek, a famous source of fossils from that time. Layers of sediment quickly covered the remains, preserving delicate details. In this fossil, scientists can even see scales on its back and impressions of its eyes.

The fossil had been sitting in the Field Museum for years. An amateur collector found it and donated it to the museum. At first researchers thought it was a known species, but a closer look showed it was a different animal altogether.
why_it_matters: This discovery shows that old fossils in museums can still hold surprises — and that young scientists can make real discoveries.
